Topics · One God, one message

What proof do I have beyond how I was raised?

An honest test: the Quran asks proof of its own first, and calls you to think alone or with one friend.

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْبَصَرَ وَٱلْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْـُٔولًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And do not pursue[745] that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those [one] will be questioned.

Translator's notes

[745] i.e., do not assume and do not say.

Quran · Al-Isra 17:36

Translation

I tell you that every idle word that men speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgment. For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”

Original · Ancient Greek

λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶν ῥῆμα ἀργὸν ὃ λαλήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ἀποδώσουσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ λόγον ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως· ἐκ γὰρ τῶν λόγων σου δικαιωθήσῃ, καὶ ἐκ τῶν λόγων σου καταδικασθήσῃ.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 12:36-37

World English Bible

What we think we know comes in kinds: what we have seen, what we heard from people we trust, what we are used to. Most of a life is the third, and that is not a fault in itself. But the verse sets a clear line: do not follow what you have no knowledge of, for your hearing, sight and heart will be asked about. So each person asks: where does my knowledge end, and where does my habit begin? Any reader, from any path, can start there.

A question for you

Where has most of what you believe come from?

If you sayFamily and surroundings
ThenThat is true of most people and no fault. The question is what you do with it now.
If you sayMy own search and experience
ThenThen you have something to test. Notice too what you wanted to find when you searched.
If you sayI am not sure
ThenAn honest start for the next step.

Part 2 of 3

﴿قُلْ هَـٰذِهِۦ سَبِيلِىٓ أَدْعُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ ۚ عَلَىٰ بَصِيرَةٍ أَنَا۠ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَنِى ۖ وَسُبْحَـٰنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "This is my way; I invite to Allāh with insight, I and those who follow me. And exalted is Allāh; and I am not of those who associate others with Him."

Quran · Yusuf 12:108

What separates a faith of habit from a faith with sight? The verse names a way "with clear sight", and it is not only the Prophet's: "I and whoever follows me". The Quran does not ask its followers to follow without looking. Whoever wants to believe is asked, by this verse, to see. The measure does not change between those born to a faith and those who came to it yesterday.

A question for you

If you could not say "this is how I was raised", what would your first reason be?

Part 3 of 3

﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَعِظُكُم بِوَٰحِدَةٍ ۖ أَن تَقُومُوا۟ لِلَّهِ مَثْنَىٰ وَفُرَٰدَىٰ ثُمَّ تَتَفَكَّرُوا۟ ۚ مَا بِصَاحِبِكُم مِّن جِنَّةٍ ۚ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ لَّكُم بَيْنَ يَدَىْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "I only advise you of one [thing] - that you stand for Allāh, [seeking truth] in pairs and individually, and then give thought." There is not in your companion any madness. He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment.

Quran · Saba 34:46

Where do you begin? The verse gives one counsel: stand before God in twos or singly, then reflect. Notice what it does not say: it does not say gather in crowds. A crowd has a mind of its own, and people in one do not think as they do alone. The method is to step away, alone or with one honest friend, and think in a way worthy of your sincerity before God. That is no one faith's request. It is what this app asks of its reader too.

A question for you

What makes thinking alone hard?

If you sayWorry about what I may find
ThenAn honest worry. It may help that Abraham asked for his heart to be at rest, and was not turned away.
If you sayMy family would feel betrayed
ThenThinking is no betrayal, and it stays between you and God. No one asks you to tell anyone anything.
If you sayI have no time
ThenThat is honest too. Ten minutes is enough, and nothing is waiting for you if you don't.

The same in the other books

Restraint in the eye is good, good is restraint in the ear, in the nose restraint is good, good is restraint in the tongue. In the body restraint is good, good is restraint in speech, in thought restraint is good, good is restraint in all things. A Bhikshu, restrained in all things, is freed from all pain.

Buddhist texts · Dhp 360-361

Max Müller, 1881

Translation

He who answers before he hears, that is folly and shame to him.
